findings.reason: the node must be told that wiring the unlink into the release path (itself the deliverable) is required, or its gate passes on a direct `crew gc --run` call while every promotion keeps leaking.
findings.text: §11's Why says "single-run gc is the path every promotion and release takes", but `garbage_collect` has exactly one production caller, the `crew gc` CLI command at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1915`; the promotion/release path (`_release_run_workspace` and `_release_worktree_whole`, `reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:337-425`, `reckon/crew/routing.py:1343-1392`) never calls gc, so a fix confined to gc's `run_id` branch would still be reached by no release

findings.reason: a negative control aimed at a branch the tested path never executes measures nothing, so the node needs a control that removes its own unlink.
findings.text: §11 declares "The negative control restores the run-id skip, and the first case fails", but the first case releases a run's worktree; if the unlink is added where the write paths point (a call from `promotion_release.py`, as the missing caller above requires) restoring gc's run-id skip changes nothing on that path and the control stays green

findings.reason: a node editing `run_store.py` would leave the aborting read in place, and its "no added failure" gate on files importing `reckon.run_store` would confirm nothing about the defect.
findings.text: §12 sends the node to `reckon/run_store.py`, but the record it describes is `docs/state/<project>/runs/<run_id>.json` (`ledger.run_path`, `reckon/ledger.py:890-895`) and the cited message "cannot read run … Expecting value: line 1 column 1" is raised by `_read_run` at `reckon/ledger.py:1265-1278`; `run_store.py` only decodes SQLite columns and never reads a per-run JSON document

findings.reason: half the stated contract (skip everywhere except this run) is unmeasured, so a node could satisfy every case by skipping the damaged record unconditionally.
findings.text: §12's deliverable says "Only a promotion of that run itself is refused", but its done-when tests only that another run's promotion succeeds beside the damaged record; nothing measures the refusal

findings.reason: an implementable section with no followup is never queued, so the work the plan declares is unreachable.
findings.text: §11 and §12 are declared `implementable` but the followups list ends at f-tchhab-009 (§9), so neither new section has a dispatching invocation and nothing in the plan reaches them

findings.reason: the plan simultaneously says §9 is finished and queued to be built, so a dispatch of f-tchhab-009 rebuilds landed work.
findings.text: the same declaration map marks `s9` done while its dispatching followup f-tchhab-009 (snapshot line 214) is still `data-status="open"` and recommends `/reckon-build the-crew-home-has-a-bound §9`, even though `c-close-s9` records §9 landed

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11's negative control restores the gc run-id skip while its first case exercises the promotion/release path the skip does not reach, and §12's done-when never tests its own "only a promotion of that run itself is refused" clause.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections send gate logs and the §11 host measure to the run directory and land evidence in `docs/evidence/archive/the-crew-home-has-a-bound-landed.html`, both durable paths.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two new test filenames name behaviour (`test_a_released_worktree_takes_its_index.py`, `test_a_damaged_run_record_stops_only_its_run.py`) and no plan label, ticket number or changelog prose appears in the added text.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11 asserts a caller that does not exist ("single-run gc is the path every promotion and release takes"), and §12 names `reckon/run_store.py` as the module to change although the truncation it describes is read and reported by `reckon/ledger.py`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11's three bullets describe one mechanism (unlink the released tree's index) with its liveness invariant and an operational reap, and §12's deliverable is one read-tolerance change.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §11 and §12 are declared `implementable` in the section declarations (snapshot line 24) but no followup invokes either, and §9 is declared done while its dispatching followup f-tchhab-009 is still open.
